name: Dipylidium caninum

taxonomy.rank_note: Reference groups can include multiple species. Protozoan higher-rank systems differ; the lineage is provided without forcing every clade into a class rank.

morphology: Eggs occur in packets, often containing multiple six-hooked embryos; individual eggs are roughly 35–40 µm.
Proglottids resemble cucumber seeds or rice grains and have paired genital pores.

transmission.detail: Flea larvae acquire eggs and develop cysticercoids; swallowing an infected flea transmits the tapeworm.

life_cycle.detail: Flea larvae acquire eggs and develop cysticercoids; swallowing an infected flea transmits the tapeworm.
Egg packets or proglottids in stool or perianal material.

hosts: Definitive: dogs and cats, occasionally humans, especially children. Intermediate: fleas, occasionally chewing lice.
distribution: Worldwide where infected pets and fleas occur; human infection is uncommon.
clinical_significance: Often mild; segment passage and perianal discomfort may prompt investigation.
specimen: Egg packets or proglottids in stool or perianal material.
diagnostics: Inspect packets at 100× and individual embryos near 400×; examine segment morphology when available.
differential_diagnosis: Annotate packet and individual egg as different object types; do not count a packet automatically as one biological egg.
review_status: Source-compiled educational content; not independently clinically validated

annotation_guidance: Record specimen, stage, stain, objective/total magnification, pixel calibration, source image and reviewer certainty.
Native crops of 200–650 pixels do not determine biological size. Retain µm-per-pixel calibration before resizing.
Split training, validation and test data by patient/specimen; keep related crops in the same split.
Keep damaged or ambiguous objects uncertain. Molecular confirmation of a mixed specimen does not assign every pictured object a species.
